Telangana to introduce 10+2 system in all state-run schools from 2027-28 to prevent dropouts, says CM Revanth Reddy
points: The Telangana government will introduce a 10 plus 2 education system in all the state-run schools from the next 2027-28 academic year, extending school education up to Class 12 on the lines of Kendriya Vidyalayas, chief minister A Revanth Reddy announced…

Currently, school education till Class 10 is overseen by the School Education Department, with the 10th-grade Secondary School Certificate (SSC) public examinations conducted by the Telangana Board of Secondary Education.
The next two years are called Intermediate Education and are governed separately by the Board of Intermediate Education (BIE).

Under the proposed new structure, education will be divided into three stages: primary education from nursery to Class 4, secondary education from Classes 5 to 8, and senior secondary education from Classes 9 to 12, all governed in a single system.

Revanth Reddy directed the department officials to make all necessary arrangements for implementing the new system from next year as part of a broader initiative to overhaul the state's education sector.

items.title: Newer, stricter PUC norms likely including digitally signed results from vehicle emission standards
points: India’s pollution-under-control (PUC) testing system could see tighter safeguards against manipulation, with a proposed amendment to vehicle emission-testing standards requiring testing equipment to digitally sign results and transmit them directly to a…

The October 2026 amendment to the Automotive Industry Standard (AIS)-137 (Part 8), issued under the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, proposes introducing hardware-based security features in petrol and diesel vehicle emission-testing equipment to ensure that…
Under the proposed framework, gas analysers and smoke meters will have to incorporate a dedicated Trusted Platform Module (TPM 2.0) security chip to generate and store cryptographic keys.

Every valid emission test will have to be digitally signed within the instrument before its results are transmitted to the Pollution Under Control Certificate (PUCC) server through the machine’s own SIM or eSIM connection.
The existing digital PUC system links test results to the VAHAN database, with NIC-developed testing software implemented in 31 states, according to the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.

Lakshmi Surya Prabha, and others took part.

During the meeting, the committee decided to earmark 10 to 25 grants from a pool of 200 Faculty Research Grants for postgraduate students undertaking research projects independently of their mandatory dissertations.

According to a release by the university, the initiative aims to encourage postgraduate students to pursue additional research, develop scientific inquiry skills and gain experience in research design, data collection, analysis and scientific reporting.
The committee discussed the introduction of courses in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Digital Health for undergraduate and postgraduate students.

items.title: Rs 80 Lakh Cash Seized From Car In Indore, 2 Detained
points: Police seized Rs 80 lakh in cash from a car in Indore on Wednesday and detained two people who claimed to be farmers in this connection, an official said.
Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police Amarendra Singh said the cash was found during a search of the suspicious car in an empty field behind a shopping mall in the Kanadiya police station area.
Two car occupants, identified as Tilok Gami (52) and Manoj Gami (44), were detained, he said.
The police officer said the two suspects are residents of the Bagli area of neighbouring Dewas district and are farmers.

According to Singh, during interrogation, the two men claimed the money came from Suresh Patel, a resident of Indore, and was the proceeds from the sale of land in the Barkheda area of Dewas district, but they were unable to produce any documents to…
He said the police seized the cash as per rules and informed the Income Tax Department about the recovery.

items.title: Direct tax collections rise 14% to ₹17.5L-cr
points: The gross direct tax collection in the current financial year (up to November 10 of FY27) increased 14.02% to ₹17,50,285.89 crore compared to ₹15,35,076.31 crore in the same period of the previous fiscal year (FY26), data released on Wednesday said.
After refunds, net direct tax revenue surged by 11.76% to ₹14,41,978.91 crore in FY27 (up to November 10) compared to ₹12,90,204.10 crore in the same period last fiscal year.
Total refunds in the said period of 2026-27 were ₹3,08,306.98 crore as against ₹2,44,872.21 crore in the corresponding period of 2025-26, registering a 25.91% jump, official data said.

Net collections from corporate tax (CT) saw a 17.84% increase to ₹6,31,959.53 crore in 2026-27 (up to November 10) as compared to ₹5,36,285.79 crore collected during the same period of previous financial year.
Net revenues from non-corporate tax (NCT) during current period saw a modest 5.3% growth to ₹7,55,944.96 crore as against ₹7,17,922.31 crore in the same period of previous year.

items.title: Gorakhpur-bound train derails in Kanpur, no casualties
points: No casualties were reported in the incident, senior police and railway officials said.
Around 300 passengers were travelling in the four affected coaches, they said.
"Chauri Chaura train [15003] bound for Gorakhpur from Anwar Ganj departed from platform number 7 at around 5.03 p.m..
As it moved out of the station, coaches B-4, B-5, B-6 and B-7 derailed, triggering panic among passengers," Commissioner of Police Raghubir Lal told PTI.
It was the second derailment incident reported in Wednesday (November 11, 2026).
Earlier in the day, five coaches and the engine of the Kolkata-Sairang Express derailed at Digaru near Assam's Guwahati, leaving four persons injured.
Deputy Commissioner of Police (East) Satyajeet Gupta said the derailment occurred at around 5.07 p.m.
All were safe and had been shifted to platform number 1, where arrangements for refreshments and a special train were being made for their onward journey, Mr. Gupta said.

items.title: Govt prohibits lithium-ion battery black mass exports
points: The government has prohibited the export of lithium-ion battery black mass with immediate effect to retain critical minerals for domestic recycling, an official said.
The move aims to keep scarce minerals such as lithium, cobalt and nickel within the country, he added.

The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) prohibited the export of lithium-ion battery black mass through a notification issued on November 10, placing the item in the prohibited category, the official, a spokesperson for the commerce and industry…
Black mass is the powdery material obtained by shredding end-of-life lithium-ion batteries and battery manufacturing waste.
Exporting black mass generated in India diverts this valuable secondary resource abroad, while domestic recyclers have, in some cases, had to import material to meet their requirements, he said.
The prohibition is intended to ensure that black mass generated in India is recycled and refined within the country.

items.title: Keralam Police Arrest Road Accident Accused After 16 Years On The Run
points: An accused in a 2010 road accident that claimed two lives in this coastal Keralam district has been arrested after being in hiding for 16 years, police said on Wednesday.

The state police said in a statement that the accused, who had been hiding in Tamil Nadu for the last 16 years, was arrested by a team from the Pattanakkad police station near the Thanneermukkom Bund road here after he came to Keralam recently.
In 2010, a vehicle driven by the accused hit two people fatally near Thumboli, police said.
Police received a tip-off about the accused, who was living under a fake name and address, on Diwali day, the statement said.
On the instructions of the district police chief, a special team was formed comprising Cherthala DSP Manjulal, Pattanakkad SI Dominic Mathew, SI Ratheesh and senior civil police officer Arunkumar.

items.title: Environmental, social costs of Vizhinjam port railway tunnel to be higher than anticipated
points: The proposed tunnel between Balaramapuram and Vizhinjam to provide rail connectivity to Vizhinjam International Seaport has triggered serious environmental and land stability concerns in the region.
Drawing on more than three decades of field experience, Mr. Nandakumar said most stretches of the proposed alignment are likely to pass through geologically weak terrain.
Beneath the top layer of laterite, the subsurface is expected to comprise of decomposed lithomargic clay interspersed with hard rock in some locations.
Such formations, according to him, are unsuitable for a tunnel carrying container trains weighing several tonnes.
He warned that the impervious concrete tunnel structure, laid at a depth of around 30 metres, could act as an underground barrier, disrupting the natural movement of groundwater.
The project in its present form could destabilise the region and may disrupt the livelihoods of millions of people living along the Balaramapuram-Vizhinjam corridor.
He urged the government to reconsider the tunnel proposal and instead opt for an overland railway alignment after establishing its economic viability.

items.title: Ioniq P Is Hyundai's Next SUV For India: Details
points: Hyundai is working on its first-ever dedicated electric SUV for the Indian market, and it is currently known by the name He1i.
It is going to be a sub-4-metre EV and is likely to be called Ioniq P by Hyundai.
The Hyundai Ioniq P, as mentioned above, will be a sub-4-metre electric SUV that will rival the likes of Tata Punch EV and Kia Syros EV in the segment.
The upcoming Ioniq P is based on Hyundai’s Electric Global Modular Platform.
E-GMP platforms dedicated to small cars, derived from the K1 platforms, are called E-GMP (K).
The mid-range variants will get a 42 kWh battery pack, while the long-range variants will either get a 49 kWh or a 51.4 kWh battery pack like the Syros EV.
These battery packs will offer a real-world driving range of anywhere between 300–450 km.
The Hyundai Ioniq P is almost production-ready, and Hyundai is expected to unveil the final product to the world at the upcoming Bharat Mobility Expo next year.

items.title: Thinking about buying the dip in HDFC Bank? Here are the pros and cons.
points: After its merger with HDFC Ltd in 2023, the combined entity became the world's seventh-most valuable bank, with about 120 million customers and more than 177,000 employees.
HDFC Bank stock has underperformed the Nifty 50 over the past year amid concerns of a growth slowdown and pressure on its net interest margin (NIM).
Anup Bagchi took over as CEO and managing director from Sashidhar Jagdishan on 27 October.
HDFC Bank has been one of the most consistent performers on Dalal Street, clocking a 20% compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) for over two decades.
Net profit has expanded at a 19% CAGR over the past five years, with the NIM (%) in the mid-40s and the return on equity (RoE) averaging 14.7%.
The bank's net NPA has never crossed 0.5% of total advances.
The balance sheet is strong, with a total capital adequacy ratio (CAR) of 18.87% against the regulatory requirement of 11.9%.
The tier-1 CAR was a little over 17% in Q2FY26.

items.title: Public concerns persist over poor air quality levels in Edayar industrial area
points: Elected representatives and residents of wards near the industrial area in Kadungallor and Eloor have been repeatedly complaining about the continuing odour and air pollution.
They have now raised the issue with the Chief Minister V.D.
“We have urged the Chief Minister to conduct a comprehensive inquiry into the polluting sources in the industrial area.

Despite bringing up the issue on several occasions, the Pollution Control Board has not been able to act tough against the violators,” alleged Abdul Riyas C.A., member of Eramam North ward in Kadungalloor panchayat.
Officials of the Environment Surveillance Centre of the PCB in Eloor said they have initiated a probe into the complaint.
However, the air quality levels in Edayar measured by private monitoring platforms had shown Air Quality Index (AQI) in the range between 120 and 168 for nearly 10 days in October and November.
As per the standards prescribed by the Central Pollution Control Board, an AQI of 0-50 is considered ‘good’, 51-100 ‘satisfactory’, 101-200 ‘moderate’, 201-300 ‘poor’, 301-400 ‘very poor’.

items.title: Drug peddlers adopt innovative methods to conceal contraband as surveillance tightens in Kochi
points: With the enforcement agencies intensifying surveillance against drug trafficking, peddlers are resorting to innovative methods to conceal and transport narcotic substances, going by recent seizures in and around Kochi.
From banana to jaggery and air coolers, traffickers are now concealing drug consignments in everyday commodities, posing fresh challenges to the police and other enforcement agencies.

In the latest seizure revealing the “innovative modus operandi”, the Ernakulam Rural police arrested an award-winning 31-year-old farmer suspected to be running a drug network under the cover of his agriculture ventures.
Videos of the accused showing methods to conceal drugs inside banana bunches were allegedly recovered from his mobile phone.
Last week, the Railway Protection Force (RPF) seized 37.7 kg of suspected ganja during an inspection of a train after it arrived at Aluva station.
In September, the Kochi City District Anti-Narcotics Special Action Force recovered 1.980 kg of suspected MDMA hidden inside an air cooler and a tower fan in a car.

items.title: National Drugs Act's stringent restrictions cannot override personal liberty, says Supreme Court
points: Keeping an accused behind bars for more than six years without the trial even beginning amounts to “punishment in itself”, the Supreme Court has held, terming the state of affairs “unacceptable” and reminding courts that even the rigours of special laws…
The bench was categorical that the stringent restrictions under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act cannot override the constitutional guarantee of personal liberty.
The court noted that the accused, Arshdeep Singh, had been in custody since May 16, 2020, and although charges were recently framed, the trial was yet to commence.
It pointed out that in such a case, the rigours of Section 37 of the NDPS Act must yield to Article 21 of the Constitution, which protects the right to personal liberty.

Setting aside an Allahabad High Court order from July 28, 2025, which had rejected Singh’s second bail application, the apex court directed his release on bail subject to conditions imposed by the trial court.

items.title: Army weighs posting Agniveers to RR units in Jammu and Kashmir
points: The Indian Army is reviewing the feasibility of posting Agniveers who have completed their four-year tenure to Rashtriya Rifles (RR) units specialising in counterterrorism operations in Jammu and Kashmir (J&K), officials familiar with the matter said on…

This includes the 25% of Agniveers selected on merit for permanent service, as well as those offered a two-year extended tenure and another opportunity to join as regular soldiers under the revised Agnipath scheme unveiled last week, the officials said.

The proposed move is significant as Agniveers have so far been excluded from extra-regimental postings, despite serving in regular infantry units deployed along the Line of Control in J&K, and in the hinterland.
RR units comprise soldiers drawn from different battalions of a particular regiment (say Jat or Rajput), as well as the armoured corps and artillery.
The changes in the Agnipath scheme were cleared by the Cabinet and unveiled by Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani on November 4.

items.title: Non-oil goods make up 15% of India’s Russia imports in first half of FY27
points: Nearly 15% of India’s $47.28 billion imports from Russia in the first half of 2026-27 comprise items other than crude oil and petroleum products, according to latest government data.
India imported coal, coke and briquettes worth $2.56 billion in H1 (April-September) of 2026-27, about 36% jump as compared to $1.89 billion in H1 of 2025-26.
In the first half of current financial year, India’s import of vegetable oil from Russia jumped over 42% to nearly $1 billion, compared to about $700 million in the same period of previous year.
India’s import of Russian pulses in just six months of 2026-27 surpassed total imports of the commodities in 12 months of 2025-26, which was valued at $81.15 million.

items.title: Bribery accused govt official reinstated at same hospital, Supreme Court questions Bihar
points: A government hospital official arrested on charges of demanding a bribe was sent back to the same hospital and the same post after his suspension was revoked -- a decision that has now drawn the Supreme Court’s scrutiny even as it restored his bail in the…

Taking note of what it called a “disturbing feature”, the court questioned how the official, who was arrested and spent 15 days in judicial custody in connection with the bribery case, could be reinstated and posted to the same hospital, in the same position.

“There is one disturbing feature which we should not ignore…This aspect shall be looked into by the state at the earliest,” said a bench of justices JB Pardiwala and Manmohan, directing the Bihar government to take appropriate steps in accordance with law.

The court’s observations came while setting aside a Patna High Court order that had cancelled the bail granted to Vishwa jeet Singh, an administrator at the government-run Sadar Hospital in Samastipur.

items.title: India slips 5 spots on climate change index
points: India has experienced a decline in the Climate Change Performance Index, falling from prior high rankings.
The country now sits at 28th position due to rising greenhouse gas emissions and energy use.
While India has made significant strides in renewable energy, the overall performance remains low.
Comparatively, Pakistan, with lower emissions, is ranked just above India at 26th.

items.title: Pollution's hidden health cost: Dirty air may also raise diabetes risk, global review finds
points: Recent findings highlight a concerning connection between PM2.5 air pollution and an increased risk of type 2 diabetes, showing that every 10 microgram per cubic meter rise in PM2.5 could boost diabetes risk by 10% to 16%.
Notably, South Asian communities, particularly in India and Bangladesh, may face a 9% heightened risk.
This underscores the urgency for improved air quality management to mitigate metabolic diseases, although definitive causation remains unestablished.
